title: A New Musical Chapter
story:
After returning from military service, j-hope was ready to open another chapter in his musical journey. In 2025, he introduced fans to three new digital singles: “Sweet Dreams,” “MONA LISA,” and “Killin’ It Girl.” Each song had its own atmosphere, sound, and story, revealing different sides of his artistry.

The first release was “Sweet Dreams (feat. Miguel),” which came out on March 7, 2025. It was a pop R&B song about the desire to love and be loved, expressed through a dreamy, heartfelt serenade. The track featured American R&B singer Miguel, an artist whose music j-hope had listened to since he was young. He later shared how happy and deeply moved he was to collaborate with someone he had admired for so long.

The song also marked a new creative experience for j-hope. While working on it, he participated in a song camp for the first time. He found the process more enjoyable than he had expected, and during his stay in Los Angeles, he created many songs. Before the official release, he surprised the audience by performing “Sweet Dreams” live during the opening night of his HOPE ON THE STAGE world tour in Seoul on February 28 – just one week before the song was released.

“Sweet Dreams” also made its mark on the U.S. charts. It debuted at No. 66 on the Billboard Hot 100 and reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Digital Song Sales chart.

Just three weeks after “Sweet Dreams” was released, on March 21, j-hope unveiled his next single, “MONA LISA.” This hip-hop R&B track celebrated the unique qualities that make someone captivating. Inspired by Leonardo da Vinci’s famous masterpiece, the song playfully compared an irresistible person to the Mona Lisa. Its message was that true charm does not come simply from external beauty, but from the special qualities that make each person different.

“MONA LISA” continued j-hope’s impressive Billboard Hot 100 run, reaching No. 65. It also debuted at No. 1 on Billboard’s Digital Song Sales chart. 

The music video for “MONA LISA” placed the performance at its center. Surrounded by a setting reminiscent of a modern art gallery, j-hope moved through the space as if he himself were a work of art. The choreography included gestures inspired by looking at and photographing a masterpiece, while the camera movements and lighting highlighted his precise footwork and expressive dance style.

The third single, “Killin’ It Girl (feat. GloRilla),” arrived on June 13, 2025. This hip-hop track captured the excitement of falling in love at first sight. Its minimalist arrangement gave plenty of room for j-hope’s rhythmic delivery, while American rapper GloRilla brought her bold energy to the collaboration. The song moved between a hip-hop-influenced verse and a more pop-oriented chorus, creating a catchy contrast.

Fans also received a second version of the song on the same day: “Killin’ It Girl (Solo Version),” featuring only j-hope’s vocals. This version put the focus entirely on his delivery and interpretation, offering a different way to experience the track. He performed the song live for the first time during the Goyang concerts of his HOPE ON THE STAGE tour on June 13 and 14.

“Killin’ It Girl” made history for j-hope on the Billboard Hot 100. It debuted at No. 40, giving him his highest solo position on the chart at that point. It was his eighth solo entry on the Hot 100, making him the K-pop soloist with the most entries on the chart. With this release, all three of his 2025 solo singles had entered the chart: “Sweet Dreams” at No. 66, “MONA LISA” at No. 65, and “Killin’ It Girl” at No. 40.

But these were not the only Billboard Hot 100 achievements j-hope celebrated in 2025. Earlier in the year, he had joined Don Toliver and Pharrell Williams on “LV Bag,” which debuted at No. 83 on the chart. Then, in November, he collaborated with LE SSERAFIM on “SPAGHETTI,” which entered the Hot 100 at No. 50 and returned for a second week at No. 89.

Together with “Sweet Dreams,” “MONA LISA,” and “Killin’ It Girl,” these collaborations brought the total to five Hot 100 entries featuring j-hope in 2025 alone. This was a record for a Korean solo artist in a single calendar year. “SPAGHETTI” also became his ninth career Hot 100 entry, further extending his record as the K-pop solo artist with the most appearances on the chart. By then, he became the BTS member with the most individual Hot 100 entries.

The three solo singles were later brought together in a special release called “Charm of HOPE,” which came out on July 11, 2025. Instead of a conventional album package, it was presented in a key-ring-shaped format that could be tapped against a smartphone using NFC technology. Each version featured one of the three songs, turning the releases into a distinctive collectible.

Together, “Sweet Dreams,” “MONA LISA,” and “Killin’ It Girl” showed how comfortably j-hope could move between different musical moods. He could be soft and romantic, playful and stylish, or bold and full of energy. The songs also reflected his growing confidence as an artist who enjoys exploring new sounds, working with musicians he admires, and finding fresh ways to express himself.

This was not simply a return to music after a long break. It was another step forward in a journey that keeps expanding, with j-hope continuing to discover new possibilities while staying true to the creativity, rhythm, and unmistakable character that have always been his own.
surpriseDescription: A little glimpse into the world of “Charm of HOPE”! Enjoy the concept film celebrating j-hope's three 2025 solo releases.

challenge.question: Which of j-hope’s three 2025 solo singles achieved his highest position on the Billboard Hot 100?
challenge.explanation: “Killin’ It Girl” debuted at No. 40 on the Billboard Hot 100, higher than “MONA LISA” at No. 65 and “Sweet Dreams” at No. 66. It became j-hope’s highest-charting solo song on the chart at that time.
